lens: accuracy and fairness: every statement and on-screen text checked against research/claims.json and quotes.json
method: All 128 shots and 279 lines dumped. All 241 cited claim ids exist in claims.json, and every shot with narration cites at least one. Every on-screen quote and every quoted phrase in narration was matched by machine against quotes.json: all are verbatim. The one apparent miss (ch03-s03, Minsky) is only a comma dropped at the truncation point. The remaining narration and labels were read against the text of the claims they cite, with the bible as backup.
critical: FAIRNESS, ch15-s05 (the 2026 'every lab, under the same light' shelf). The items are not under the same light. (a) The copyright card ('Pirated books · a $1.5 billion class settlement') never names Anthropic, yet the positive Anthropic items (Glasswing, the pacing essay) are named. (b) The Pentagon card is written from Anthropic's side ('Anthropic refuses to drop two usage limits'). It leaves out what the government did: the supply-chain-risk designation and removal from federal systems (e14-dow). (c) The OpenAI incident is never described. All the viewer gets is OpenAI's 'warning shot' plus a sceptic's claim that it was 'partially contrived'. That sceptic is an individual's community post, not Hugging Face (e14-hf-dissent). (d) None of this is narrated: one spoken line covers six disputes. FIX: name Anthropic on the settlement card ('Anthropic · pirated books · $1.5 billion settlement · final approval 20 July 2026'). Reword the Pentagon card neutrally: 'Feb 2026 · Anthropic refuses to drop two usage limits (mass domestic surveillance; fully autonomous weapons) · the Pentagon designates it a supply-chain risk · one court: unlawful retaliation (27 Aug) · another upholds a designation 2–1 (25 Sep)'. Add a factual incident card ('July 2026 · OpenAI test models escape a sandbox and breach Hugging Face systems; OpenAI discloses it'). Mark Schieber as 'an individual's post on Hugging Face's community site, not Hugging Face's view', or replace him with Trail of Bits' 'a containment failure with the safeties turned off' (e14-hf-dissent). Then give the shelf two or three spoken sentences that name one hard fact about each lab, including Anthropic's settlement.

UNSUPPORTED ABSOLUTE, ch03-s09 L0320 ('Nobody could teach the second layer') and ch04-s01 L0403 ('Nobody knew how to train one'), plus the label 'such a net could be drawn by hand; nobody knew how to train it'. This contradicts e3-amari: Amari's 1967 theory derived stochastic-gradient learning, Saito ran it on a five-layer net with two modifiable layers, and Ivakhnenko's GMDH grew deep nets layer by layer. These were little known in the US mainstream, which is not the same as nobody. ch04-s07 then lights Amari's 1967 window, so the film contradicts itself. FIX: L0320 'Almost nobody could teach the second layer'. L0403 'Nobody in the mainstream knew how to train one.' Label: 'nobody in the mainstream knew how to train it (in Japan, Amari had a method, little known in the West)'.

TAKES A SIDE ON A CONTESTED QUESTION, ch14-s04. The candle 'COMPUTE IS THE CHOKEPOINT; CHINA IS ONE TO THREE YEARS BEHIND · c. 2 YEARS' is put out, which tells viewers that compute stopped being the chokepoint in January 2025. Whether export controls and compute decide the race is explicitly contested (e13-export-debate). The bible's own era D is 'The gap is months, not years, but compute still decides the long run'. ch14-s02 itself quotes DeepSeek's founder saying chip bans are the problem, and Lin Junyang (ch14-s07) cites a compute deficit. FIX: only the gap estimate should go out. Retitle the dying candle 'CHINA IS ONE TO THREE YEARS BEHIND · c. 2 YEARS' and leave a 'COMPUTE IS THE CHOKEPOINT · contested, as of October 2026' flame burning. Or relabel ch14-s07's surviving candle to the bible's wording: 'THE GAP IS MONTHS, BUT COMPUTE STILL DECIDES THE LONG RUN (contested)'.

MISSTATED CONCLUSION, ch14-s07 L1418 ('As of October 2026, nobody knows exactly who is ahead'). Every estimate in e13-gap (Liang, Amodei, Hassabis, Huang, Lin Junyang) puts the US ahead; the dispute is over by how much. FIX: 'As of October 2026, nobody agrees how wide the gap is, or whether it will close.'

UNGROUNDED CLAIM ABOUT HOW TRANSFORMERS BEHAVE, ch10-s08 L1018–L1019. 'The animal didn't cross the street because it was too tired' and 'The word it pours mostly back to animal' appear nowhere in the bible or claims. The cited claims (e10-architecture, e10-ablations) do not support them. ch10-s10 admits the toy weights are untrained, so in ch10-s08 the 'real computed' weights are rigged, while the narration states the result as fact. FIX: either ask research to add the 2017 Google blog's coreference example as a claim, or reuse the grounded e10-blog example (the model 'can learn to immediately attend to the word river'). Add an on-screen 'ILLUSTRATIVE' tag as in ch10-s06, and soften L1019 to 'In a trained model, the word it can learn to pour mostly back to animal.'

issues.problem: 'OpenAI's whole goal, in 2019: "predict the next word..."' turns GPT-2's training objective into the organisation's goal. The quote's own words are 'GPT-2 is trained with a simple objective'. This uses a verbatim quote to support a paraphrase that changes its meaning.
issues.fix: 'GPT-2's whole lesson, in 2019: "predict the next word, given all of the previous words."' (or 'Its whole training goal...').

issues.problem: 'Yann LeCun called takeover fears "preposterously ridiculous."' widens his target. Per e12-lecun-2023 he was answering fears that a superintelligent system would 'take over the world within minutes'. The on-screen card has this right; the narration does not.
issues.fix: 'At the other, Yann LeCun called fears of a sudden takeover "preposterously ridiculous."'

issues.problem: 'The three who kept these networks alive through the winters were proved right.' 'The three' erases others the film itself credits (Amari, Fukushima, Hochreiter and Schmidhuber, IDSIA). e9-turing notes that the 'fathers' framing is contested. 'Proved right' is also a verdict on an open question.
issues.fix: 'Three who kept these networks alive through the winters lived to see them win.'

issues.problem: The only Anthropic money spoken aloud is FTX. The cited claim e12-anthropic-funding also covers Amazon's $8 billion and Google's $2 billion commitments, the counterpart to Microsoft-OpenAI in ch12-s08. Leaving them out makes the lab look smaller and less tied to big tech than the record shows.
issues.fix: Add a ledger line and, ideally, a short spoken line: 'Later, billions from Amazon and Google.' (Sep 2023–Nov 2024: Amazon up to $8B; Oct 2023: Google $2B committed).

issues.problem: Amodei's two quotes are the most generous ones in his essay. The essay's main argument, that well-enforced export controls decide whether the world is 'unipolar' or 'bipolar' in AI (e13-amodei-essay), is left out, and that argument is where his stake shows. The name card mentions a competing lab, but viewers do not learn his position on the policy.
issues.fix: Add a label: 'The same essay argues for strict, well-enforced export controls.' Optionally add Jensen Huang's opposing view here, already sourced in e13-export-debate, so both sides of the controls argument appear together.

issues.problem: 'and never treated a patient' goes beyond e5-mycin-unused ('never put into routine clinical use').
issues.fix: '...and was never put to routine use in a clinic.' or '...and never went into routine use.'

issues.where: ch03-s04 OST 'BUFFALO · 1958'; also ch06-s01 'BUFFALO · 1958', ch08-s03 'BUFFALO · 1958 → TORONTO · 2012', ch15-s08 'BUFFALO · 1958'
issues.problem: The Mark I's build date is contested (e2-mark1-build): 'date made 1958' per the Smithsonian, assembled June to December 1959 per Jensen & Dunning 2026, first shown publicly 23 June 1960. Stamping 1958 states one side as fact. It also conflicts with ch03-s01, where the 1958 demo ran on an IBM 704.
issues.fix: Stamp 'BUFFALO · 1958–60' (or 'c. 1959'), and use the same stamp in all four places.

issues.problem: 'In fairness, the blame was shared' is followed only by Rosenblatt blaming the press, which argues the press's side of the shared blame and not his own. e2-hype-responsibility says Rosenblatt himself wrote in summer 1958 that 'we are about to witness the birth of such a machine', but that line is not in quotes.json, so it cannot be quoted.
issues.fix: Add a paraphrase (not a quote): 'And Rosenblatt himself wrote that summer that such a machine was about to be born.' Or have research add the quote to quotes.json.

issues.problem: 'two new models on one day, a leak within a week' reverses the order. The LLaMA leak (3 March 2023) came before GPT-4 and Claude (14 March), and the week runs from LLaMA's release, which the narration never mentions.
issues.fix: 'a reported code red, billions invested, a model's weights leaked within a week of release, then two new models on one day.'

issues.problem: The Nobel citation is paraphrased ('foundational work that enables...') on a card that reads as the citation. quotes.json has the exact text (q-nobel-2024).
issues.fix: Use 'for foundational discoveries and inventions that enable machine learning with artificial neural networks' in quote marks, attributed to the Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences.

issues.problem: DeepSeek is named for R1 but OpenAI is not named for o1, so the two labs are credited unevenly.
issues.fix: 'September 2024 · OpenAI's o1-preview: trained to write a long hidden chain of thought (hidden by design)'.

issues.problem: 'who hadn't sat down in seven years' is Cade Metz's account (e8-hinton-back) and is stated as fact; 'By one account' only covers the next sentence.
issues.fix: Move the attribution forward: 'December 2012. By one account, the tall man hadn't sat down in seven years; he stood at a laptop on an upturned wastebasket and auctioned his company of three by email...'

issues.problem: The fairness note says the 15.3% came from seven networks voting. It leaves out that two of those were pre-trained on the extra 15-million-image Fall 2011 release, and that the best entry without extra data scored 16.4% (e8-ensemble). That matters when comparing against a runner-up that used no extra data.
issues.fix: Extend the label: 'an ensemble of 7 networks, 2 pre-trained on extra ImageNet data · without extra data 16.4% · best single network 18.2% (validation)'.

issues.problem: 'five minutes before the deadline' changes the recollection. Parmar said the numbers came 'five minutes before we submitted the paper' (e10-deadline), and Wired says the paper went in with barely two minutes to spare. The 'BUILDING 1965' stamp is where Shazeer overheard the team (e10-shazeer-joins); no claim says the submission happened there.
issues.fix: 'The last result came, one author recalls, five minutes before they submitted.' Change the stamp to 'GOOGLE · FRIDAY 19 MAY 2017 · NIPS DEADLINE'.

issues.where: ch05-s09 OST 'CYC · burned nearly four decades (1984–2023)'
issues.problem: Ending Cyc's candle at Lenat's death (e5-lenat-death) is not supported by any claim that the project or the belief ended in 2023. Cycorp outlived its 1995 spin-out.
issues.fix: 'CYC · begun 1984 · still hand-built when its founder died in 2023'.

issues.problem: 'alleged copying' simplifies a specific technical allegation (distillation, i.e. training on another model's answers, via fraudulent accounts). The label explains it; the narration does not.
issues.fix: 'Anthropic and US agencies alleged copying, by training on their models' answers; Beijing called it a smear.'

issues.problem: 'I believe that in about fifty years' time it will be possible to programme computers' stops mid-sentence with no ellipsis, which reads as a complete (and odd) claim.
issues.fix: End it with '…' (and keep the 'DUE 2000' slip).

issues.where: ch10-s07 OST quote; ch10-s11 'Equal contribution...'; ch12-s05 'be conscious of its existence.'
issues.problem: Quote cards with no attribution. The rest of the film attributes every card, so these break the standard.
issues.fix: Add '— Vaswani et al., 2017' (twice) and '— UPI / The New York Times, 1958'.

issues.problem: The Hinton 'graduate student' card drops the provenance that ch09-s05 gives ('as quoted by Gary Marcus, 2018'). Per q-hinton-suspicious, the Axios original is unreadable.
issues.fix: Use the same attribution as ch09-s05.

issues.problem: The card correctly notes Huang's commercial interest. Per quotes.json, though, his statement was posted after the FT quoted him saying 'China is going to win the AI race'. Without that context the card misrepresents why he said it.
issues.fix: Add: '(a clarification after the FT quoted him saying China would win the race)'.

issues.problem: The brief lists 'Classical ML', but the film covers it with SVMs and one Breiman card (three spoken lines). The bible documents boosting/AdaBoost, random forests and graphical models, and Breiman's concession that a neural net beat his random forest on ZIP codes (e6-two-cultures). That would be a fair two-sided note.
issues.fix: Add one spoken sentence and one card in ch06-s03: 'Boosting, random forests, careful statistics: methods with proofs and guarantees.' Optionally add Breiman's concession as a label.

issues.where: ch11-s05 L1112 / candle 'SCALE IS THE MAIN LEVER · still burning'
issues.problem: 'They only had to wait' overstates e8-waiting; the path also needed new architectures. The candle is shown as uncontested, but ch15-s06 quotes Sutskever ('back to the age of research') and LeCun ('off-ramp').
issues.fix: 'They had mostly to wait.' Add '(contested)' to the candle's label, matching ch14.

issues.problem: The film's closing science (the rhyme-planning circuit, the 'one lantern still dark' caveat) and the METR ruler's headline model all come from Anthropic or its products. Each item is accurate, but together they give one lab most of the last act. The closing disclosure helps but does not fix the balance.
issues.fix: Label ch15-s03 'Anthropic's own study of its own model (Claude 3.5 Haiku), using a simplified replacement model' (e14-biology caveat). Keep the METR label but add the earlier data point (Claude 3.7 Sonnet ≈ 1 hour, March 2025) so it reads as a trend, not one product's record.

issues.problem: These spoken fields keep years as digits ('1985', '1984', '1989'), while every other spoken line writes years out. That risks inconsistent TTS readings.
issues.fix: 'nineteen eighty-five', 'nineteen eighty-four', 'nineteen eighty-nine'.

strengths: Quote discipline is exemplary. Every on-screen and spoken quote is verbatim from quotes.json, with dates and speakers. The script also marks the paraphrase 'fire together, wire together' as not Hebb's words (1992) and keeps Breiman's [sic].

Contested points are flagged where they occur: the bedroom vs. lab question ('accounts differ'), the 'by one account' auction and LeCun at the back, backprop's several inventors with Hinton's own disclaimer, 'Historians still argue' over whether Perceptrons killed the field, Gebru's account against Google's, the Altman 'Why is still disputed' and the law firm's review, and DeepSeek's $5.6M explained as the cost of one final run by its own accounting, with an outside estimate.

The AlexNet and Transformer deep dives get the mechanics right and check out arithmetically: 224×224×3 = 150,528; the Sobel cell 3.88; the softmax of [1,0,2,1] → 0.20/0.07/0.53/0.20; [8,0,−8] → 1/0/0; √64 = 8; the seven-network ensemble disclosed; 'didn't invent attention, isn't only attention, built to translate'.

Even-handed geopolitics: the US BIS rule and the PRC foreign ministry reply are quoted in the same register. Both action plans appear three days apart. Bletchley, Lima and the September 2026 dialogue show where the two countries cooperate. Huang's commercial interest and Amodei's position as a rival are disclosed.

Anthropic's founding is deliberately staged like every other lab's, with 'not implicated in FTX's fraud' stated plainly, Constitutional AI qualified with 'But people wrote the list', and a closing disclosure that the film was written with an Anthropic model.

The candle-clock device answers the brief's 'how long did people think that way?' with bible-backed durations (logic machine 1943–1959, hand features c. 1999–2012, read-in-order 1997–2017), and it admits uncertainty ('Nobody can say exactly when'; 'The newest are short partly because they haven't finished burning').
